subject: Proposed p50/p95 regional outlier handling + degraded-mode SLAs for migration week
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rizvi <sana@fintegrate.com>, Fintegrate Ops <ops@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintegrate.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed p50/p95 regional outlier handling + degraded-mode SLAs for migration week

Hi Sana (and team),

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed, Fintegrate’s planned data migration in the US-west region during the week of Dec 6 carries a predictable spike in short-lived API latency while customer traffic warms across caches. To keep your production experience stable, I’m proposing a temporary, well-scoped deviation to the hosted API SLOs for that week. This is an operational exception (not a permanent contract change) and includes auditability and automated rollback.

Summary of the proposal:
- Duration: 2026-12-06 00:00 UTC -> 2026-12-12 23:59 UTC
- p50 commitment: unchanged (<= 80ms)
- p95 commitment: we request a relaxed measurement during the window — measure p95 over rolling 5-minute buckets (rather than 1-hour) for regional aggregation for the US-west cluster only. This allows transient bursts to be isolated to migration window artifacts.
- Fallback mode: if p95 exceeds the temporary threshold for 3 consecutive 5-min buckets, we will automatically route 30% of traffic to a dedicated model pool (no customer tokens are moved), preserving correctness while absorbing tail latency.
- Observability & audit: we will expose a live dashboard and ship a daily evidence CSV and a final migration-week evidence package.

Why this is safe and reversible:
- The p50 target remains the same so most requests see no change.
- Rolling 5-min buckets are strictly for measurement/exception classification; production routing and throttles remain in place.
- Auto-fallback is reversible and monitored; we will not scale the dedicated pool beyond agreed burst caps without explicit approval.

Attached: a short playbook and historic evidence from similar migrations (anonymized).

Ask: please confirm acceptance of this operational exception and that Procurement can sign the one-week addendum (we’ll send a DocuSign link). If you want, we can gate the change behind a canary on Dec 6 (first 2 hours) and then open to the rest of traffic.

Thanks,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

Subject: Re: Proposed p50/p95 regional outlier handling + degraded-mode SLAs for migration week

Thanks Michael — appreciate the detail. A few quick clarifying questions before we sign off: 

1) Can you confirm the temporary p95 relaxation absolute threshold (ms)? Our compliance team needs a hard number to approve the measurement change.
2) For the auto-fallback: what guarantees do we have about request ordering and KV-cache coherency when 30% of traffic is routed to the dedicated pool? We can't tolerate stale responses on certain endpoints.
3) Please include the daily evidence CSV in a secure S3 share and make sure audit logs show the exact routing decisions (time + reason) — Procurement will need these for our post-mortem.

If you can answer the above and provide a DocuSign addendum, Procurement will review. We prefer a short canary on Dec 6 before applying the relaxed measurement more broadly.

Sana
VP, Platform Ops
Fintegrate

Adding a couple of technical constraints from the infra side (cc'd Sana so she's aware):

- Measurement detail: the temporary p95 threshold we recommend is +300ms above the standard p95 threshold (i.e., if standard p95=350ms, temporary p95 threshold becomes 650ms). This delta keeps normal tail noise within an expected band while preventing unlimited slippage.
- Cache coherency: the dedicated pool will run the same model and KV-cache warming procedure. We will mark routed requests with an x-redwood-routing-id header; we recommend Fintegrate validate idempotency on write endpoints during the canary.
- Canary proposal: start 6am PST on Dec 6 for 2 hours at 5% traffic, then 30% for the next 4 hours, and escalate only if no read/write anomalies are detected.
- Logs & audit: we will stream per-request routing metadata to a secure S3 prefix (role-based read for Fintegrate) and produce a human-readable daily summary.

If that's acceptable I can prepare the pipeline to enable the auto-fallback and the measurement adjustment as a single config flip; both are reversible.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
